description: All release-age policy lives here, and this preset is extended LAST in renovate.json for that
reason. minimumReleaseAge is a plain scalar, so the last matching rule wins; the two rules
below that remove a soak have to beat every earlier setter, including the 1/7/30-day
per-update-type ladder in github>ppat/renovate-presets and override-calver's flat 14 days.
Keep this entry last in extends, and keep new release-age rules in this file rather than
somewhere earlier where an unrelated preset can silently outrank them.

packageRules.description: delay patch updates to 7 days (from 1 day)
delay minor updates to 30 days (from 7 days)

description: Images this repo builds itself (docker.io/ppatlabs/*) are adopted as soon as they are
published: no release-age soak, on any update type. PROBLEM: a soak exists to let someone
ELSE's release be found broken by someone else before this cluster takes it. For an image
we build there is no such someone else -- the build is ours, it has already passed its own
repo's CI, and the soak only delays our own change from reaching the cluster. This is not
a claim that first-party images are safer or better tested than upstream ones; it is that
the thing a soak waits for does not exist for them.
No matchUpdateTypes, deliberately: version updates and digest refreshes alike, major
included. Enumerating types would leave whichever type was not listed soaked by whatever
set it last -- the 1/7/30-day per-update-type ladder from github>ppat/renovate-presets for
obsidian and obsidian-tools, override-calver's flat 14 days for openclaw -- and a soak
under internalChecksFilter 'strict' is a suppressed branch, not a late PR (see the digest
rule below for that mechanism).
'minimumReleaseAge: null' is a workaround spelling, not a semantic assertion: null is the
unset value, and checkMinimumReleaseAge (util/minimum-release-age.ts) skips the check when
the value is falsy. Read it as 'zero'; Renovate has no literal zero for this option.
Both spellings of the name are listed: the registry-prefixed form the kubernetes manager
emits for the image reference AS WRITTEN in the manifest (docker.io/ppatlabs/<name>), and
the bare form a '# renovate: datasource=docker depName=...' annotation would produce. A
matcher that matches nothing raises no error -- 'ppatlabs/{/,}**' was inert for two years
for exactly that reason (#3795). Note the idiom takes NO slash before the brace.
